facts.statement: Ageleodus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that lived during the Paleozoic era.
facts.quote: Ageleodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish from the Paleozoic era.

facts.statement: The genus Ageleodus is known from two species, and all known fossils consist of isolated teeth.
facts.quote: It is known from two species, both of which are based upon isolated teeth.

facts.statement: Ageleodus lived between 372.15 and 303.7 million years ago, spanning from the Famennian to the Kasimovian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Kasimovian (372.15 to 303.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ageleodus belongs to the parent group Holocephali.
Ageleodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The species A. altus was described in 2006 based on fossils from the Carboniferous of Australia.
facts.quote: A. altus was described in 2006 from the Carboniferous of Australia.

facts.statement: A study of 382 specimens revealed that Ageleodus exhibited strong heterodonty, with teeth varying widely in length and the number of cusps.
facts.quote: A study of 382 specimens from the site showed the strong heterodonty of this genus, which varies widely in tooth length and cusp number.

facts.statement: Although generally considered a chondrichthyan, Ageleodus has not been classified into any known order or family.
facts.quote: While generally considered a chondrichthyan, it has eluded classification into any known order or family.
